steps.text: Beat together butter, white sugar, brown sugar, peanut butter, salt, baking powder, and baking soda in a stand mixer until smooth. Scrape down the sides of the bowl and beater with a spatula. Add egg and mix for about 1 minute. Slowly mix in flour with the mixer on low speed. Scrape down the sides of the bowl and beater. Continue mixing until dough comes together, about 30 seconds.
Form dough into a ball, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for 2 to 3 hours.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone baking mat.
Portion cookie dough into equal-sized balls and place on the prepared baking sheet. Use damp hands to roll dough into smooth balls. Stamp each ball with a fork in a criss-cross pattern.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden, about 10 minutes. Let cookies sit on the baking sheet briefly before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

review.reviewBody: I followed the recipe exact, only using super chunk peanut butter because that was all I had on hand. They turned out absolutely beautiful, just like peanut butter cookies are supposed to look. SIDE NOTE: My issue with making cookies lately is with the heat, they get.......weird, even with how fast the family can eat them. This cookie turned out perfect and it was a small enough batch that I didn't have to worry about the cookies "wilting" in the heat. My husband called me this morning and said that not only did they hold up well in Tupperware for his lunch but his co-workers liked them, too.

Easy to make and good flavor. I add 1 tsp vanilla and about 1/3 cup more peanut butter. I think the peanut butter that starts with a “J” makes them taste the best. I have made the dough and used it right away, and other times I put in the fridge to harden, then take it out and make 1 1/2 inch cookie balls, then put in freezer. I can then bake them whenever I want. I don’t even use a fork to make the cross cross pattern on top.,I just put the cookie balls in a greased cookie sheet and while they bake they form cracks on the top, like dry crackled sand in the dessert. I always put a 1” peanut butter cup in the middle of the cookie , as soon as they come out of the oven. I like the white chocolate peanut butter cups best. If you keep these in an air tight container, they stay semi-firm. If they are exposed to air, they get soft overnight.,

I added some shredded coconut to my 2nd batch and they came out delicious! (Made 24 total, 12 in each batch) Also, I was a little impatient, so I didn't roll them into nice little balls NOR did I let them sit in the fridge. Right after mixing I scooped I them into balls using a 2 spoon method, just eyeballing the size, did the criss cross with my fork (my favorite part, I don't know why!) and baked right away. Next time I'll give myself a little more time and let them sit, maybe that enhances the flavor like it does for chocolate chip cookies? Anyway, good cookie! The whole house smelled delicious! Easy recipe, will make again.

I made these three times (although the first time I really messed up) the next time I followed the recipe exactly except I did not flatten them. I kept them in a ball and when they were done I place a chocolate kiss in them. They came out perfectly.
Made these and added dark chocolate chips. Also I didn't have time to refridgerate and they turned out delicious. Probably a little thicker than the recipe.

I used 1/4 C almond butter; 1/4 C peanut butter--both without sugar; I used 3/4 Coconut sugar; 1/4 c coconut flour; 1/4 C buckwheat flour; remainder unbleached flour, which I sifted; small ice cream scoop--made 34 crisp and very delicious cookies.
Thank you for this great recipe!!

Our new favorite PB cookie! Followed recipe and added about 1/4c additional PB because I saw some others added a little extra. I got 26 cookies, baked at 380 for 14 minutes- these are perfect! Plenty of PB flavor (I saw a comment or two that felt PB was lacking- I used jif creamy) and the texture- amazing! Firm and crunchy and then chewy on the inside. I sprinkled with a little sugar prior to baking for embellishment. This recipe is a winner- and so easy to follow. Wonderful directions!
These were very good cookies. The 2nd. time I made them I doubled the peanut butter and added peanuts. Even better!

These are perfect! Excellent peanut butter flavor and are nice and crisp if you bake them about 10 or 11 minutes (which is how we like them) I just mixed the dough by hand and the cookies had a more crumbly texture than if beating with a mixer. Perfect batch size for a small family, too.
Turned out great. I doubled the recipe and added shaved chocolate and used a scoop. ThAt made 35 cookies. I will make again. I didn’t refrigerate the dough just went right on to baking.

I had to make changes to the receipt as I have a lot of food issues, but these are still great cookies. Just the Nuts peanut butter - mixed well - soy allergy All vegetable shortening - lactose intolerant Egg substitute - egg allergy - makes it vegan
No vanilla in recipe and not enough peanut butter makes for a tasteless, boring cookie!
I made these for work and everyone loved them.

The cookies spread out all over the cookie sheet. I even added an additional 1/2 c. flour because of another person's same problem. Even after the added flour and chilling the dough for 3 hours, I thought the dough was not texture was not stiff enough, but since I had already added an extra 1/2 c flour, I still gave it a try. Dissapointed
Liked this versatile recipe. I used half almond flour and half gluten free flour. I added vanilla and a tsp of instant coffee flakes. Also added mini chocolate chips to the last third of the batter.
I replaced the smooth peanut butter with crunchy and it was a treat.
For people that run into the issue that it's too crumbly, as I did, the solution is to double the amount of peanut butter.
I would use chunky peanutbutter or Planters dry roasted lightly salted peanuts.

Awesome recipe, have made many times. Made 2 additions that I personally think elevated them. 1/2c chunky peanut butter(in addition to the creamy), and 1/2c whole wheat old fashioned oats at husbands request. Also used an xtra lg egg. On parchment, no greasing necessary, and didn’t refrigerate before baking this time, but will try next time to see how well it works
